title: One MU proposal filled in one book; two accounts recorded a wait
body_html:
One MU proposal filled in one book; two accounts recorded a wait

Paper trading · 2026-10-13T18:05:49.276469-04:00

This briefing uses records through the fixed cutoff of 2026-10-13 22:05:49 UTC. The paper account snapshot was captured at 22:05:49 UTC. The mean-reversion book’s performance snapshot was at 19:19:18 UTC, just after its simulated fill; the adversary book’s snapshot was at 19:17:04 UTC, before its decision completed at 19:23:49 UTC. These are recorded snapshots, not guaranteed closing prices, and older snapshots may precede activity later that day. Book purchase prices exclude fees.

Today's lesson: Proposal, approval, and fill are different events

Keep the steps separate: the mean-reversion book proposed a $50 MU purchase, deterministic risk approved it, and then the book recorded a simulated fill. For example, 0.053191 shares × $939.88 equals about $49.99 before fees. The paper account and adversary book recorded deliberate waits instead. A submitted or approved proposal by itself is not a fill.

Portfolio review

Paper account

The paper account snapshot captured at 22:05:49 UTC showed $2,000 cash and $2,000 equity. Its earlier performance snapshot, at 19:15:48 UTC, also showed $2,000 equity and a 0% return. The paper decision was NO_ACTION with a deliberate wait for MU’s next quarterly results; it recorded no proposals. No broker fill is shown in the supplied records. The strongest recorded case against waiting was MU’s recent growth, positive cash generation, and 12.63 trailing P/E, which could mean waiting misses further recognition. These are discrete snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.

mean-reversion

The mean-reversion book began with $2,000. Its performance snapshot at 19:19:18 UTC, shortly after the recorded MU simulated fill, showed $1,950.00684292 cash, $1,999.93829844 equity, and account P&L of -$0.06170156 (-0.003085%). That is account-level performance, not a supplied MU holding return; the holding’s current price and unrealized P&L are unknown. The book proposed a $50 MU limit purchase with a $940 maximum. Deterministic risk approved it, and a simulated fill—not a broker fill—recorded 0.053191 shares at $939.88. The strongest recorded counterargument was that exceptional growth and margins may reflect a cyclical peak, while the share price was high in its admitted history and debt and peer comparisons were limited. The performance snapshot is a point-in-time record, not a guaranteed closing valuation.

mean-reversion-adversary

The mean-reversion-adversary book’s 19:17:04 UTC performance snapshot showed $2,000 cash and equity, with a 0% return. The snapshot preceded its completed decision, which also described the account as entirely in cash with no positions or open orders. The decision was NO_ACTION and a deliberate wait for Micron’s next quarterly results; it generated no proposal, so this book has no recorded deterministic risk approval or rejection and no fill. Its strongest recorded counterargument to waiting was that a small MU starter could capture further gains if recent growth, margins, and cash generation persist. The recorded objection was that those results may be unusually strong for the cycle, leaving no well-supported normalized downside basis. The separate valuation snapshot predates the decision, and no later performance valuation is supplied.

Every holding

MU — mean-reversion

The mean-reversion book holds 0.053191 MU shares at an average purchase price of $939.88 per share. Its recorded simulated fill was 0.053191 shares at $939.88, or about $49.99 of shares before fees. The holding snapshot at the 22:05:49 UTC cutoff has no current price, position value, or unrealized gain/loss. The book’s earlier account-level performance snapshot showed a small loss, but that does not establish MU’s holding-level return. The same-day proposal’s reasoning cited recent strong reported results, a 12.63 trailing GAAP P/E, a 5.55% free-cash-flow yield, and 256.3% trailing revenue growth; it treated management’s AI-demand outlook as a claim to be tested. The strongest counterargument recorded was peak-cycle normalization: margins were unusually high and MU’s cited price was at the 93.3rd percentile of its admitted history. No prior open thesis was listed; the same-day proposal supplies the recorded reasoning.

What remains uncertain

The two deliberate waits cited the risk that MU’s exceptional growth and margins could normalize. The mean-reversion proposal’s strongest opposing case was that recent primary results and positive cash generation might persist, so waiting could miss further recognition. The records do not resolve that disagreement; both decisions pointed to the next quarterly results as evidence to watch.

What to watch next

Watch for the recorded trigger: MU’s next quarterly results. The decisions identify revenue, gross and operating margins, operating cash flow, and capital spending as useful evidence about whether recent performance persists. Check the timestamps on any new valuation snapshots before describing returns; the current MU price and holding-level unrealized P&L are unknown here.

Proposal: A suggested transaction. It is not an executed trade.

Deterministic risk: A fixed policy check that can approve or reject a proposal; approval alone does not mean it filled.

Simulated fill: A recorded simulated execution in a book. It is distinct from a broker fill.

Snapshot: Values captured at a particular time. A snapshot may be older than later activity and is not necessarily a closing price.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book holdings replay fills through the cutoff; individual current prices are unknown.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
